skill_entry.name: 14. Shared state reached from a new thread, guarded by a new lock, or no longer waited for
skill_entry.trigger: Added non-comment lines under h/ or src/ show one of: (a) a new parallel region (parallel_for, parallel_for_limited, std::thread, std::jthread, std::async, worker fanout) whose body reaches a function that ran serially at BASE; (b) a new mutex, lock_guard or static mutex array with no comment naming the guarded state, where the mutated member lives in another file or struct, or a lock held over a loop whose node type lives in another file; (c) one struct hunk adds a std::atomic member and a plain member written by one function; (d) one block reads a racy getter (count_complete_gofs, an atomic load) twice, in a condition and a dependent value; (e) a software readiness predicate (name contains needed, ready, visible, depends) is narrowed or removed where another minibatch or thread writes the storage it guards.
skill_entry.procedure: Apply the do-not-fire list first; take HEAD from the review row. (a) Parallel region: reach the callee through lambdas and template bodies; list the members it writes and their owner; grep the callee for a lock or atomic; combine nested regions to decide whether two executions reach one object. (b) New lock: name the mutated member and its file, the owner's existing mutexes, and the mutex each other mutator takes; separate the mutating part from the waiting part. (c) Atomic/plain mix: list readers and writers per member with their thread. (d) Double read: find the sibling block that caches the value and the base-branch fix. (e) Narrowed predicate: check the removed wait did not move into a callee; compare the consumer's read width with the predicate. Report object, writer thread, reader thread, protection file:line or NONE, precedent; the race is Insufficient data (runtime).
skill_entry.question: Which thread writes this state and which thread reads it at HEAD, and does the lock, atomic or wait that separates them live in the object that owns the state and cover every path that mutates it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Applied before the steps. A mutex whose comment names state declared in the same file, including a lock held over a loop there (tron-1722 hwkv_mutex; PR 2777 placer.cpp, no comment). A member mutex over the owner's own container (tron-2469 qalloc_mutex over device->queues; tron-2875 n->mtx). Atomics added alone with no caller outside their header (tron-2693 kv_saves_). A plain member of a thread_local object (PR 2777 device_placer). A whole-loop lock once the author states the reason (PR 2233). A fanout with one device per iteration and no added lock (tron-2475, tron-3756); a rewrite of an existing region (tron-4077). A wait that moved into a callee, and hardware DMA waits (tron-2008): index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch owns those. Memory-order choices. Observed-race claims. A missing test for a new primitive (4614385493).
skill_entry.finding_shape: Question form (default, his own initiative): "I assume you <lock `<mutex>` for the entire loop | made `<members>` (and only these) atomics> because <someone could update `<structure>` during the gather | `<reader>` runs on a different thread>?" Statement form (only when answering an existing thread): "`<callee>` (<file:line>) is not <locked | waited for>. So concurrent <calls | minibatches> on the *same* `<object>` would <contend on `<member>` with no lock/guard protection | read `<storage>` while `<writer>` writes it>." Placement form (the head already carries a caller-side lock): "IMO it would be better to add a mutex member to `<owner>` and take it inside `<callee>`; the wait only compares per-caller values, so the lock can end after `<mutating call>`." Double read: "see line <L> where the value is cached."
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, never 'nit'. Of the six rows, three are replies inside a thread another reviewer or a bot opened (3275212298 to axch 3274515787; 3125517302 and 3970590653 to cursor[bot]). On his own initiative he used the question form in two of three rows (2983867856, 3406007619); default to the question form and use the statement form only when answering an existing thread. His own words on the six rows: 'I'm inclined to balk at this a bit', "this is probably 'fine' just because I don't think we're actually parallelizing across the **same device**, right?", 'may be acceptable', 'I would still ultimately defer to @mcherba', and he labels his own reading ('based on my read of the code', 'I _think_'). Adjacent rows outside the six: 'I do think there's merit to this complaint' (2983833171, PR 2233, src/pos/worker.cpp:808, a reply to cursor[bot] on an early release inside prepare_hwattn_cmds) and 'I think this is a legit concern' (3156090573, PR 2565, full.hpp:858, a shard-ordering reply to cursor[bot]). The one blocking row (3970590653, reader no longer waits for a writer) stayed COMMENTED on 2026-09-09 until the fix fe516bb512 landed, then APPROVED on 2026-09-14 at df9b800181; he never used CHANGES_REQUESTED. He defers lock placement in driver code to the file's owner by @-mention and does not block on it.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (every acquirer of the mutex, the sibling block that caches the getter, the comment above the mutex); callers (every other mutator of the member and the mutex each takes, every caller of the parallel region including generated code under ingest/); other files (the callee definition under src/, the owning struct header, the FUSE registration in src/pos/device.cpp, the consumer accessor in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp); commits (base branch log for an earlier fix of the same pattern); the review row's commit id (the inline comment's commit id is re-anchored by GitHub). Runtime evidence is needed to confirm a race and is normally unavailable: write Insufficient data (runtime) for the race and report the protection gap. The dropped-wait branch (e) is worded from the merged code comment at 9653307d68:common.hpp:957-960 and the pasted GPT text on 3970590653; Wade's own text on that thread is only 'I asked GPT to evaluate this... it agrees:', so present that branch as a check Wade acted on, not as his wording.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: shared state reached from a new thread, guarded by a new lock, or no longer waited for

Setup. HEAD = the commit of the review row: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/reviews --jq '.[]|select(.user.login=="Wado-posi")|[.submitted_at,.commit_id]|@tsv'`. Never take the inline comment's commit id: GitHub re-anchors it to a later head when the line survives a push. If `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails, read files with `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD --jq .content | base64 -d` and the diff with `gh pr diff N --repo positron-ai/tron`; without network write `Insufficient data (no network)`. Save the full text of every file that declares a mutex or atomic the diff adds, and the definition file of every callee inside a new parallel region.

1. Trigger grep over production files, comment lines and the threading primitive excluded:
   `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src ':!h/tron/threading.hpp' | grep -v -E '^\+\s*//' | grep -n -E '^\+.*(parallel_for|std::thread|std::jthread|std::async|std::mutex|lock_guard|unique_lock|scoped_lock|std::atomic|fetch_add)'`
   `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -v -E '^[-+]\s*//' | grep -n -E '^[-+].*(_needed|_ready|ready\(|visible\(|depends)'`
   Map hits to HEAD file:line: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,","); n=substr(a[1],2)+0; next} /^-/{next} {if ($0 ~ /^\+.*(parallel_for|std::thread|std::mutex|lock_guard|std::atomic|fetch_add|_needed|_ready)/) print f":"n": "substr($0,2); n++}'`
   Expect 10-30 hits on a loading PR. List t/ and threading.hpp hits as context only. Apply the do-not-fire list to every hit now; a covered hit is listed as context and not run through steps 2-7.
2. Parallel region. When the body is a template or lambda parameter (`body(e)`, `f(ix)`), the region has no callee of its own: `git -C WT grep -n '<region fn>' HEAD` over the WHOLE tree (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs emits generated C++ callers) and take the lambda at each caller as the body. Follow lambdas through at most two levels; beyond that take the entry points named in the PR body ("Changes" bullets) and in existing review threads, and state which levels were not read. Callee definition: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\b<callee>\(' HEAD -- h src`; body: `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p'`; write every member written (`dev->`, `q->`, push, assignment) and its owner; `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p' | grep -n -E 'mutex|lock_guard|atomic'` (empty = unprotected). Combine every enclosing region before deciding whether two executions reach one object: an inner device-disjoint loop (`dev_idx = map.mask[i]`) reaches the same device twice when an outer fanout runs it once per expert. Record the outermost new region and the object key of the innermost call.
3. New lock. Read the comment on the mutex: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<decl-3>,<decl>p'`. If it names a state declared in the same file or struct, stop for this hit. Otherwise the state = the member the locked call mutates (step 2). Acquirers: `git -C WT grep -n '<mutex>' HEAD -- h src`. Other mutators: `git -C WT grep -n '<member>' HEAD -- h src`; walk each up to its callers until a lock_guard or none is found and record the NAME of the mutex (two different mutexes on one member is a finding of its own). Wait split: `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p' | grep -n -E 'wait_for|usleep|delay_ns|while|do \{'`; record (i) what the wait reads and (ii) what it compares against; a wait that writes, pops or resets nothing and compares shared state with values the caller got from its own enqueue (`start_ch`, `end_desc`) can run outside the lock. House convention: `git -C WT show HEAD:<owner header> | grep -n 'std::mutex'`.
4. Lock over a whole loop (node or entry type declared in another file): `git -C WT grep -n '<mutex>' HEAD -- <file>`; per acquirer note whether it mutates the looped structure; `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<lock-3>,<lock+2>p'` for a reason comment; the thread that runs the loop comes from the author's reply or the PR thread.
5. Atomic/plain mix: per new member `git -C WT grep -n '<member>' HEAD -- h src t`; tag each hit with its function and thread (src/pos/worker.cpp = TX worker; `git -C WT grep -n -E '&[A-Za-z_]+::<member>' HEAD -- src` = a pointer handed to tron::fuse::stats, read on the FUSE thread; an object declared `thread_local` has no cross-thread reader and the plain/atomic mix is not reported). The atomic set must equal the set of members with a reader on another thread.
6. Double read: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(count_complete_gofs|dma_complete)\(\)|^\+.*\.load\('`; enclosing block: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /\{$/ {n=NR; s=$0} END{print n": "s}'`; warning comment: `git -C WT grep -n -B2 -A2 '<getter>' HEAD -- h | grep -i -E 'race|async'`; sibling cache: `git -C WT grep -n -E '= [a-z_.]*<getter>\(\);' HEAD -- h src`; earlier fix: `git -C WT log --format='%h %an %ad %s' --date=short -S'<getter>' BASE -- <file>`.
7. Narrowed predicate: first `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep -n '<removed wait name>'`; a `+` line inside a function the hunk now calls means the wait moved, and the check stops for that hit. Then `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep -n -A14 '<predicate>('` and read old and new side by side; consumer read width: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'scaled_v|entire page|whole page|interleaved' HEAD -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp`; tests on the predicate and whether they pre-initialize the shared storage (which hides the case): `git -C WT grep -n -l '<predicate>\|poison\|NaN' HEAD -- t/`.
8. Report per hit: object, writing thread, reading thread, protection file:line or NONE, precedent (sibling line, earlier commit, member mutex in the owner). Question form by default; statement form only inside an existing thread; placement form when the reviewed head already carries a caller-side lock (never the unprotected statement then); `Insufficient data (runtime)` for the race itself.

final.widen_delta: Frontmatter description: append 'shared state reached from a new thread without a lock, locks placed away from the state they guard, racy getters read twice, readiness predicates narrowed so a reader no longer waits for a writer'. Words used here: add 'TX worker: the per-device thread in src/pos/worker.cpp that builds FPGA commands', 'FUSE stats thread: the thread that reads counters registered through tron::fuse::stats', 'racy getter: a function whose declaration or a nearby comment says its value changes under asynchronous work (DMA completion)', 'readiness predicate: a function (token_ix_needed, *_ready) that decides whether a consumer may read storage another producer writes; hardware DMA waits (wait_for_xfer_blocks, wait_for_hbm_*) are not readiness predicates here', 'owner of the state: the struct or file that declares the mutated member', 'review row: the commit id GitHub stores on the review, the head Wade read; an inline comment's commit id is re-anchored to a later head when its line survives a push'. The thirteen questions become fourteen; add question 14 = the check's question. New heading 'Checks on thread ownership' holding check 14 after check 13. 'How Wade words a finding': add two bullets. (1) A thread-model concern starts from his own assumption in question form ('I assume ... because ...?') and he labels his own reading ('based on my read of the code', 'I _think_'); a change is asked only after the fact and the consequence are stated, and the statement form appears only inside a thread someone else opened. (2) He defers lock placement in driver code to the file's owner by @-mention and does not block on it; he does not comment on memory_order choices. 'Report the result': add 'Never claim an observed race; report the missing or misplaced protection and write Insufficient data (runtime) for the race itself.' Setup step 1: add 'Take HEAD from the review row, never from an inline comment's commit id; when the reviewed head is absent from the worktree, read it with gh api and say so. Also save the full text of every file that declares a mutex or atomic the diff adds, and the definition file of every callee inside a new parallel region.'
